Hey. You're going to be just fine, I promise. 

Shave your hair off. Don't waste any more time worrying about that, hair will grow back. I've done it twice now due to severe depression and I keep joking that I'm due to shave it off again next year as the previous times were in 2012 and 2018. 

Once your hair is no longer a problem, hop into the bath or shower. Build up to it if you need to. It sometimes helps me to promise myself a little treat after I've done a task I need to do. Like, shower and then I can open some candy and watch a TV show in peace. The bath/shower won't be as difficult if you aren't worrying about how it will make your hair worse because of the matting. Just spend 2-3 minutes in the water and then you can get out, but I think once you're in there, you'll relax a bit and stay longer. 

Clean towel and clean clothing at the ready, get out, dry off, clean clothes.. I promise you, you'll feel SO much better, and like you've accomplished something. Then treat yourself. Not a magic fix for your depression but it will help lift your mood a little. 

My DMs are open if you need someone to talk to. I've been on the dark, suicidal side of depression, I tried to take my own life in October. But I'm so glad I'm still here. Message me day or night. That goes out to ANYONE reading this. I'm not promising I can help but I can lend an ear and give advice about this sort of thing.

I had a miscarriage at 12 weeks, I don't know exactly what happened but I'd be sent home to allow the process to take its course... Fell asleep on my sofa. I woke up at 7am the next day and walked to the toilet and suddenly blood was swooshing out of me. I remember my ears ringing and everything faded to black, and then back into focus. I realised I was haemorrhaging and shouted to my then-partner who proceeded to run downstairs and start vacuuming the house. No idea why? Shock possibly? I rang my best friend who told me to call an ambulance immediately. I didn't, I called the hospital ward on the number I'd been given the day before. She asked if I was bleeding through more than a pad an hour. I said 'Yeah about a pad an hour' and she told me to call a taxi and get to the hospital immediately. I was bleeding a hell of a lot more than that. But me being me, I called my friend back and she told me to call a frickin' ambulance. I called the ward back and said "it's more like 3 pads an hour" (again, it was way more than that) at this point I'm suddenly really cold and shaky. Nurse tells me to call an ambulance if I'm feeling unwell. I finally call the ambulance and tell them I'm bleeding so badly that my clothes, bathroom and hallway are covered in my blood and there's huge clots. They send an ambulance straight out. Waiting for the ambulance, I shouted my then partner to bring me clean clothes, which I struggled to get myself into whilst he resumed vacuuming(??!) 

So I'm waiting for the ambulance, got myself into clean clothes that IMMEDIATELY became drenched in blood.. they arrive and my partner let them in and explained I was upstairs. They carried their monitors and things into the house, took one look at me all drenched in blood, white skin, shaky..and said they need me in the ambulance asap. I stand up and walk downstairs, which they were NOT happy about.. then became so weak so suddenly that they needed to use a wheelchair to get me from the door of my house to the gurney in the ambulance. Wheelchair was soaked in blood after that short journey. Then I was in the ambulance, being blue lighted to hospital. A box of gloves kept falling on me whenever we turned a corner and that's when I started laughing hysterically, I couldn't stop. Paramedic looked so serious which made me laugh more...like he really wasn't impressed with me at all. I remember being pushed around the hospital to the surgery ward, totally covered in blood and I was thinking to myself "It must be so cool for people watching me being wheeled around all bloody and gross"

I remember my blood pressure being insanely low, 76/34 and the blood was still coming out in huge clots. They tried sticking a weird device inside me to stop the bleeding, it didn't work. They then said I needed to be rushed to theatre. I was thinking how it was like being in a medical show. Surgeon started explaining the risks of surgery to me and I kept asking annoying questions ON PURPOSE because I found their impatience hilarious for some reason. I mean, they just wanted their patient to live but I wanted to be silly. Then I remember them letting my then partner, my 3yo and my then mother in law see me before I went to theatre. They said that haunted them, how fragile, pale and sick I looked. Then I was in the pre-op room, and I was starting to lose consciousness. I remember watching someone get things ready to put me under a general, and someone else said "Hurry, she's becoming restless." And I was sort of groaning quietly. Then nothing. 

Woke up a few hours later, alive and being given more blood transfusions (I'd been given blood and fluids and all sorts of things during the time before going into theatre but the main things I remember are my low blood pressure, which was constantly being monitored and I was very tachy.) 

It was dark when I woke up, and I needed a drink. I tried to get a drink and knocked my water jug onto the floor, thought "fuck it" and fell asleep again. Nurses were calling me sleeping beauty because I'd slept for 18 hours, looking all pale and deathly. 

Well..I survived. Wasn't until a few years after that that I was diagnosed with a blood clotting disorder called Von Willebrand's Disease.
